name: Nations & the believer
about: God's judgment on nations, and the believer in them.

teachings.title: Ye are the salt of the earth
teachings.summary: People are saved by faith alone, but nations are judged by Christians' works, so America's decline comes from believers losing their savour and not turning from wickedness, which is not persecution for righteousness' sake.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 37**, God promises that the wicked shall be cut down like grass, while those that trust in the Lord and do good shall dwell in the land and be fed.

This is a crucial detail in the Christian life, and the fate of our families and nation. The conditional understanding, that those who trust in the Lord, His people, the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus, are given the opportunity to have life, in abundance, though obedience to the commandments of God. To do good.

We are given eternal life by faith in Christ Jesus alone. Trusting God. But our lives on this earth are judged by the good that we do.

People are judged by faith. Nations are judged by Christians' works.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

It is a popular verse, quoted often from pulpits across America. And it shows that there is a solution to the chaos and depravity affecting our society, and that solution is not found in consuming political commentary or voting. It is turning towards God and away from evil, as His people.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Salt is a preservative that keeps meat from spoiling. It not only stops the rotting, but improves the flavor and texture of it when cooked. When tried by the fire.

We are to be that salt, and when the Christian loses his savour, we see that we become useless, and are left to be trodden down, and rightfully so.

This is in contrast with the earlier verse;

**Matthew 5:10–12**
*Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.*

We often hear Christians complain about being vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked, and who treat the inevitable trodding down caused by our lack of commitment and separation, as persecution for righteousness sake. They are not the same.

In fact, many Christians live as the world, not doing good that they may dwell in the land, and act surprised when the wicked prosper and our nation is flooded with strangers, bringing their idolatry and paganism with them.

They act as though they are being persecuted by politicians and corrupt leaders, while in reality we are the cause.

We become fearful and resentful, fretting about evildoers and being envious of the workers of iniquity.

We ignore God's prescriptions for what ails us, and so we forsake the promises of safety and provision He has given us.

teachings.title: No political solution for a spiritual problem
teachings.summary: A sinful land gets many oppressive rulers, and God gave Christians, the salt of the earth, the job of preserving the nation through revival in the church and soul winning, not the ballot box.
teachings.text:
*For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged*.

There is no political solution for a spiritual problem. The iniquity and sin in a country results in *many princes,* that is more and more oppression and rules and rulers.

It could also mean instability and high turnover. Frequent coups. Parties switching off power every few years. Revolution after revolution. A sinful people get the leadership they deserve.

While a wise king, filled with the fear of the Lord and the understanding and knowledge that follow, his rule shall be established and stand, and is the joy of a righteous people.

Reminder that God has given the responsibility of preserving our nation to Christians.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

Revival begins in the heart of believers, in the pews of their local church, in the highways and hedges, at the doorstep of the lost.

Not at a ballot box, not on cable news, or a podcast or YouTube comments section. It doesn't begin in a Telegram chat, or social media post, or at a rally for a politician.

Christians are the salt of the earth, preserving their land, prolonging the state of a land.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

teachings.title: America the tall cedar
teachings.summary: Like Assyria the tall cedar, America will fall, and when depends on whether believers keep their savour by preaching, soul-winning and separation.
teachings.text:
God's message to Pharaoh, showing the Egyptian king the power of God against Assyria, is a pretty apt message for the 4th of July.

What other nation has been made as fair than America? It has shot up like the cedars, its roots by great waters. *He hath shot up his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height*.

This message is fitting and will come to pass on this nation. When is entirely up to saved believers. We are the salt of the earth, but so many have lost their savour. Good for nothing but being trampled underfoot.

Churches that don't preach the gospel, pastors that don't preach the whole word of God. Members who don't go soul-winning. Who live like the world in all they do. Zero separation unto the things of God.

If the uncircumcised nations of heathens fell, if Israel was destroyed for their iniquity, imagine how much greater America's fall will be.

It will be biblical.

*Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls! For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate. Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.*

God bless America.

teachings.title: Though Noah, Daniel and Job were in it
teachings.summary: The righteous stave off a nation's judgment for a time, but when it comes only the saved are spared, though God often spares their families for His purposes.
teachings.text:
Then the Lord gives Ezekiel His word, that when God sets out to destroy a land as wicked as Israel, that even if *Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it,* He would only save them themselves from it.

The illustration that 3 renown righteous men would not be sufficient to save a nation that had backslidden to the point of Judah in this day. No children. No remnant. Only the righteous men themselves.

This establishes a few things that we may know from other scripture. One that, as Abraham argued with the Lord concerning Sodom and Gomorrah, that the presence of the righteous is generally sufficient to stave off judgement, at least for a time. We are the salt of the earth. We preserve the world unto judgment, but eventually it isn't sufficient and God's wrath comes due.

Second, when this judgment comes, only the saved are spared. Only those made righteous by faith in the blood are not appointed to wrath.

Third, it is interesting that Daniel, a contemporary of Ezekiel has, by this time, been noticed of God. It isn't clear that Ezekiel himself may know of Daniel, although the youth was made a president of the Babylonian empire early in captivity. But the Lord knows, and knowing we'd know, he is held up as an example.

Finally, there is a tendency of God's mercy, that when it isn't a final judgment, when it serves His needs, He will save the family of the righteous from that judgment. As 8 were saved by the righteousness of Noah. As Lot's wife (almost!) and his daughters are saved from Sodom. As the remnant of sons and daughters mentioned here in **Exikiel 14**.

*For thus saith the Lord God; How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast? Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters*

The remnant was left for His sake. For His name's sake and the city where He had chosen to place His name. To ensure the line of David continues and that Jerusalem stands, awaiting the Messiah that would come from both, Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: We are the righteous remnant
teachings.summary: Believers are the salt that withholds God's judgment, and when the salt loses its savour the remnant will be taken like Lot before His wrath is poured out.
teachings.text:
Beginning in **Isaiah 1**, the major prophecy set in pre-captivity Judea, the Southern Kingdom, Isaiah preached in the 8th century BC, in a similar timeframe as the minor prophets and Kings and Chronicles we have recently covered, and so the themes are familiar.

Israel is gone astray, into adultery with foreign gods, idols, and wickedness. Blood of the innocent shed, the poor defrauded, the widow uncared-for. The sickness of the rulers, even in Judah, has corrupted the Temple as well. God is displeased, and is warning of His coming judgment.

Here, in Isaiah, God is pleading with the people, *Let us reason together*. The Lord has made it clear, from Moses to their present that if they walked in His commandments, they would be His people, and He would be their Lord and the land would be theirs and be blessed.

And yet they fall short, and worse, commit iniquity. Unrighteous judgment.  He cannot abide it any longer.

*Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

This calls back to the pleading of Abraham before Sodom's destruction, that if there were yet ten righteous men, God would spare the city. But it also points to our own time, and the coming judgment.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men*.

We are the righteous remnant. Believers are the salt that preserves the earth and withholds God's judgment. We are called to retain that savour, to be faithful and to obey the Lord's commandments, being a light unto the world.

And when the fullness of the nations comes, and the salt loses its savour, a falling away, the small remnant will be taken like Lot, spirited away by the angels of God at Jesus coming. And His wrath will pour out on the unrighteous.

But, as always, God's refining judgment will lead to the redemption of those who trust in Him. The city of righteousness will be ours. That faithful city, Jerusalem the mother of us all.

teachings.title: Turn again unto the Lord, the remnant
teachings.summary: Hezekiah preached to Israel's remnant that God's wrath could still be turned away, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 is a standing promise, so even in a wicked nation we compel men to return to the Lord.
teachings.text:
*Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria. And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see. Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves unto the Lord, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the Lord your God, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you. For if ye turn again unto the Lord, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the Lord your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.*

Hezekiah is preaching the word of God to the lost sheep of Israel. The Northern Kingdom had been made nearly desolate by the Assyrians. A remnant still remained, and Ephraim and Manasseh were yet to be wiped out. There was still time and hope for them as a nation of people who called themselves after His name. The fierceness of His wrath could still be turned away.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

This is a standing promise to Christians, from a God who cannot lie. God, who is longsuffering and merciful, Who rewards those who diligently seek him. Who runs to meet the prodigals coming home to Him.

Very apt timing, the day before our elections here in the United States. Not that a godly person is on the ballot. Not that our wicked nation deserves healing.

But as bad as the people are, and as unclean, we are to compel them to come. To turn back to the Lord, that the fierceness of His wrath be delayed, that a remnant will hear and believe, and His children will get right and sanctify themselves, so that He may forgive us our sin and heal our land.

teachings.title: His mercy endureth forever
teachings.summary: Christ is the mercy of God that endures forever, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 shows God's mercy on a humbled, praying people is the only answer to sin in a nation.
teachings.text:
Here in **2 Chronicles 7**, we see the dedication of the Temple complete, with a 7 day feast and the sacrifices made, and the people worshiping in the presence of the glory of the Lord. The fire of the Lord come down from heaven to consume the burnt offerings.

The priests committed to their service, making the offerings, even the musicians as David had instructed, with Solomon as King, presiding over all.

And the people praised God, saying *He is good; for His mercy endureth forever.*

Jesus Christ is the mercy of God which endureth forever. The grace of the Father made manifest in the Son, Who is the consuming fire come down from Heaven.

And the judgment of God upon the nations of people who call themselves by His name, one of the most quoted verses of scripture, comes in **2 Chronicles 7:14**

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

This is the only answer to the sin in the land. God's mercy. This is how we as a nation are restored today, just as this promise inspired revival in the returning Jews out of Babylon.

The Lord's mercy endureth forever. Amen.

teachings.title: If my people humble themselves
teachings.summary: God offers nations under judgment a way back, as with Nineveh, if they turn from idols and wickedness and seek Him.
teachings.text:
But with this judgement against nations, God in His mercy offers a promise;

*But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee, neither destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers which he sware unto them.*

This is repeatedly offered throughout scripture, a way to turn back the judgment against nations, to get right with the Lord.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
 *If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

This extended not just to the Israelites, but was given even to the Gentiles of Nineveh;

**Jonah 3:3-10**
*So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey. And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes. And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands. Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not? And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

God judges nations on this earth, just as He judges individuals in Heaven. And if we, like so many times in the history of the judges and kings recounted in scripture, destroy the altars and high places, smash the idols, remove the sodomites from our land, and turn from those evil ways towards the Living God, the Lord will repent of the evil He would do, and heal our land.

teachings.title: If my people which are called by my name
teachings.summary: Nations are judged by the works of those who call themselves by God's name, and the promise of 2 Chronicles 7:14 extends to every nation with Christians in it.
teachings.text:
The judgment of nations is by their works, and more, the fruit of those among them that call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land*.

This promise is extended to every nation, that has Christians living in it. And every nation on earth has saved Christians among them. Or those apostates calling themselves by His name, yet chasing idols and drunk on the fornications of their mother church.

As we watch the inevitable destruction of our nation coming, as Jeremiah did in visions from the Lord, we can relate to him, and how he felt. Yet take comfort in the fact that even in his Lamentations, he held fast to the hope of the promise of the Lord.

teachings.title: Not doing nothing: how a nation is healed
teachings.summary: A nation is healed not by sedition and outrage but by God's people humbling themselves, praying, obeying, raising godly families and winning souls (2 Chronicles 7:14).
teachings.text:
Unsaved men often criticize born again believers as "doing nothing," or that we are "weak," "afraid" or or "cowardly" because we aren't running around in panic, screaming in terror and getting sucked into reactionary spirals by the provocations and tribulations that the rulers of the darkness of this world, the spiritual wickedness in high places subject everyone to.

They rail and demand we join seditions and taking vengeance for ourselves. And they fail to notice that the more they do this, the worse the situation becomes for everyone. That they give those dark powers serving the god of this world justification for more cruelty, and make would-be allies among us more afraid of us than the wicked who oppress us.

This frustration, doubts and and impatience with God can strike even believing Christians.

But God is clear on how we save our nation and get His blessings for our people.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

Have faith. Obey the commandments. As much as possible live peaceably among men. Be a Godly husband, raise Godly children and share the gospel, winning souls. Give comfort to those morning, be a good judge for the fatherless and true widows.

This is not "doing nothing." It is hard work, or else it wouldn't be so difficult to get people to do it. Like most effective things, it requires discipline, motivation and perseverance. It's easier to express impotent outrage online.

The frustrations and provocations assailing us are how Satan tempts us, so he can accuse the saints before God. To make us sin over it, so that we can be persecuted for those sins by the powers that be. They want to avoid persecution of believers for His name's sake as much as possible, because they know that when they do, when they explicitly and clearly persecute us for our faith, directly, they lose.

The Bible says we suffer gladly for His sake we are rewarded here and in Heaven for it, and I can testify that at least as earthly rewards, it's true. And as a people, if Christians turn towards God and obeying Him, fearful for nothing except God, He will hear us and heal our land and brings blessings to all our nation, believers or not.

*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

teachings.title: Revival starts with the children of light
teachings.summary: A nation slouching toward Gomorrah fails because Christians compromise, so revival begins with believers walking in the Spirit, honest and submitted to God.
teachings.text:
So, again, the question of why we as a nation (because God judges nations here on earth), ...why as a nation are we failing, slouching to Gomorrah?

Is it the children of darkness, of wrath? Doing the unseemly things they do, not having the light within? As they flail around in the darkness?

Or is it the people who call themselves by His name, going along with it? The children of the light? Not shining the light but walking after the ways of the unsaved and unbelieving? Compromising, and so being compromised...

It starts with us. We lead revival. Not with flowery words and enabling our own sin. Not with judgment designed to puff us up, and rationalize our faults as, "at least, not as bad as those sinners over there."

We do it by walking in the Spirit. We do that by staying in the word, in prayer, in praise and thanksgiving. By being honest in our dealings. In meekly having a ready answer to our hope, which isn't in our works and good deeds, such as they are, but in Christ. By submitting to God, and His will for us. To honor our roles.

This is what brings blessings to a nation, when the people who call themselves Christian act like it, and in doing so bring others into the same light.

teachings.title: Turning toward the Lord is all we have
teachings.summary: Only Bible-believing Christians turning from their own wicked ways to God can delay the wrath America deserves; voting, shooting or vengeance are vanity.
teachings.text:
It is in the hands of Christians, Bible believing, born again sons of God, to turn away from their wicked ways, their indulgence in the world, in sin, in the subversive and perverse things we are tempted with, and turn towards God the Father, in Jesus' name.

All other methods of delaying the wrath that America deserves are vanity. We cannot vote our way out. We cannot shoot our way out. We cannot riot and murder and exact our own vengeance, and expect any relief.

There is only one path. Turning to the right or left leads to destruction. Turning towards the Lord is all we have. #IndependenceDay #4thofJuly

teachings.title: Make us a king like all the nations
teachings.summary: Like Israel demanding a king, Americans seek political overthrow, but every system is judged by God when it turns from Him, so the answer is getting people right with God.
teachings.text:
**1 Samuel 8:5**

*And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.*

This is the spirit far too many Americans find themselves in today, wanting to overthrow the current system entirely because it's leaders are corrupt and the people are wicked.

Even the Israelites, with the perfect system of God being their King, the law literally set in stone, and Godly men given power by God to judge them, still went through cycles where they failed the system, and were captured or occupied. Where their own wicked deeds brought about decades of oppression, and it's only by turning to the Lord and repenting of that evil do we see them return to prosperity.

It doesn't matter if we are a monarchy, democracy, fascist, socialist, a dictatorship... We are going to be judged by God if we turn away from Him.

That's why all of this debate about political solutions to our spiritual problem is vain and foolish. Work on getting enough people right with God and the rest will sort itself.

teachings.title: Open idolatry worse than secret
teachings.summary: God counts the open idolatry of a whole people worse than the secret cults of its great men, and judges the nation for it.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 8**, the prophet is lifted up by the hand of God, by his hair, and transported spiritually to Jerusalem, to witness the abominations of Judah.

He is shown an idol set up inside the gates, an image of jealousy.

**Exodus 34:14**
*For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God*

He sees the glory of the God of Israel, as he had in chapter 1, and He shows the prophet more abominations, including a hidden chamber filled with idols, and 70 men led by one, Jaazaniah, offering strange fire of incense to their idols in secret. In a hole in the wall, thinking they his themselves from God.

This is a wicked, hidden cult with great men of Judah involved, in secret. Our modern minds think of Masons and Jewish tunnels and attempts to hide their sin from God. Yet the Lord says He will show Ezekiel greater abominations.

He then shows him two groups of people, the women publicly "weeping for Tammuz," and men facing the East Gate of the Temple, facing the rising Sun to worship it, rather than the altar, the laver, the holy of holies therein, to the West.

They have turned their land to violence and they put the branch to their nose, they thumb their noses at God. Publicly.

We often think about the secret societies and satanic cabals that rule the nations, and the evil they do, and it is true they exist even today. But notice God finds the practices of the people, who are openly worshipping false gods worse than the things that go on in secret.

And the Lord judges the nation that turns from Him. He will not spare them or have outt upon them. He will not hear their cries.

teachings.title: Seek ye the Lord before the day of His anger
teachings.summary: Men are judged after death but nations are judged collectively on earth, so Zephaniah calls all the meek of the earth to seek the Lord before His day of wrath.
teachings.text:
God judges nations. While the judgment of man comes after our physical death (*and it is appointed unto men, once to die, but after this the judgment*).

But the judgment of nations is here on this earth, and is a collective judgment of the people in their land.

The prophets, as we have seen, are sent by God with warnings and rebuke, calling the lost to repentance, nations to reform, Kings to fear the Lord.

Zephaniah is calling the people of Judah, and ultimately all the world, to turn to the Lord in meekness, seeking righteousness.

*Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.*

He warns of the destruction that will befall all nations that have not turned towards Him, and that persecute His people. *The Lord will be terrible unto them.* The burden of the Lord upon the prophet says that men shall worship the Lord, *every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen.*

The prophecy of **Zephaniah 2** is both to the Jews of his time, but also shows that His people are not confined only to them, but of the meek and humble who believe on His name throughout the world.

And the destruction of all nations will be not only to the various nations called out here, but the wrath will be poured out on all the earth against those that transgressed against Him and His people, in the day if the Lord's anger.

The day of the Lord is coming. Christ will return in judgment.

Before the day passes, before the fierce and terrible day of the Lord come, seek ye the Lord. Before it is too late.

teachings.title: Why the wicked devour the more righteous
teachings.summary: As with Babylon against Judah, God raises up wicked nations to judge a fallen Christian nation, but those wicked nations will face His judgment too.
teachings.text:
Habakkuk was a prophet and contemporary of Jeremiah, preaching during the time leading up to and during the Babylonian captivity. He begins by saying the *burden* which he did see. Just as in Jeremiah we see that the prophets called being given the word of God *the burden of the Lord.*

**Jeremiah 23:36-40** mocks the false prophets who continually claim the burden of the Lord.

But Habakkuk sincerely carries this burden, beginning with his  crying out to the Lord in anger and frustration at the state of Judah in his day.

There is violence, strife, contention and spoiling or thefts, the law isn't being enforced and corruption keeps right judgment from being made. The wicked are prospering and are protected by the government while the righteous are victimized.

Sounds familiar.

In verse 5, God begins to respond. The Lord says He will work a wonder in the prophet's days, rising up the Chaldeans, the Babylonian empire, and they will invade Judah and possess it.

God says they are terrible and mighty, even their horses like leopards fiercer than wolves. That their armies will gather up Judah to captivity, scoff at their kings, and the cities will be destroyed by them.

God also gives Habakkuk the prophecy that the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar, shall take credit for this wonder God wrought against Judah.

*Then shall his mind change, and he shall pass over, and offend, imputing this his power unto his god.*

(This is fulfilled in **Daniel 4**, another study for another day)

Habakkuk replies, respectfully but a bit incredulous.

*Art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction. Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?*

He asks how God could use the wicked Nebuchadnezzar and the heathen Chaldeans to destroy Judah, that as bad as it is, they are still more righteous than Babylon. They make men no more than fish to be caught in nets, slaying nations, and then worship the net rather than the Almighty God who established them. Worshiping the creature more than the Creator.

*Therefore they sacrifice unto their net, and burn incense unto their drag; because by them their portion is fat, and their meat plenteous.Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare continually to slay the nations?*

He asks, what about their judgment?

It is so familiar to us, today, and likely this story resonated with believers throughout Biblical history. We decry our own nation falling from grace to judgment. We call out to God to deliver us, to punish the wicked, and set right the sins in the land. A Christian nation that has fallen away.

But when God rises up the heathen, the wicked, the Muslim and the Jew and the pagans of India and the godless of China, and we are beset from all sides by the worst, whom God has raised up, we ask how can this be that *the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he?*

But God will explain that while He may use the wicked to judge the more righteous, they too will face His judgement.

teachings.title: Nations judged by works, individuals by faith
teachings.summary: Edom and the nations were destroyed for their works, because God judges nations by their works even as He judges individuals by their faith.
teachings.text:
The final stanzas of lamentations for includes a prophecy against Edom. As we will see in Ezekiel and Obadiah, Eden was destroyed because they rejoiced and mocked the destruction of Israel. We can develop that further later when it comes, but it is something to keep in mind that the brother of Israel faced God's wrath, Just as the final chapters of Jeremiah detailed the destruction of Egypt and the surrounding nations and ultimately Babylon.

God judges nations based on their works. Even as he judges individuals based on their faith. It's an important distinction to keep in mind as we rightly divide the word of God.

teachings.title: The wine cup of God's fury on all nations
teachings.summary: God judges nations by their works while saving individuals by faith, and His fury poured on Judah and its neighbours foreshadows the judgment on end-times Babylon.
teachings.text:
In **Jeremiah 25** we see that the prophet has been preaching the word of God for 23 years, and he was not alone. Zephaniah and Habakkuk, and eventually Daniel and Ezekiel (after captivity began), are Jeremiah's contemporaries. The prophets of God trying to make strait the paths of Judah, while God uses His "servant," Babylon as the rod to lead them back to Him.

In chapter 25 we see the preaching of destruction and desolation of Judah laid out;

*Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle.*

But, the Lord says through Jeremiah that His wrath will also come to the other nations of the region, utterly destroying them as well. Babylon as an empire serving as God's tool to pour out His wrath. And Judah will be captive 70 years, saith the Lord.

But God also tells us that this desolation and destruction will come to all nations. That God will recompense them according to their deeds. God judges nations by works, even as He offers salvation to individuals by faith.

And so God gives the prophet an understanding that the wine of His fury will be poured out against them all. Both literally the nations of Egypt and Uz and Moab and Edom and the rest, and as we read on, God swears His vengeance on every nation, in that great and terrible day of the Lord.

Even as Isaiah preached. And as the revelation of Jesus Christ gave to John about the future nation with the spirit of Babylon upon it, whose destruction parallels with the destruction of Jerusalem in Jeremiah's day:

*And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee*.

Even as all hope for God's repentance is lost and Jerusalem and the other mighty nations of the time cannot escape the judgment that's upon them, God gives the hope that His wrath against His people will be short lived, and He will eventually turn that wrath against Babylon, the nation that has its spirit upon it in the end times.

teachings.title: The potter's power over nations
teachings.summary: The potter of Jeremiah 18 and Romans 9 is about nations, as God destroys some to show His wrath and His mercy on others, as with the Jews and Gentiles.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 18** begins a shift in the narrative structure, where for the past several chapters Jeremiah had made some effort to plead with God to not be too hard on Judah, and God explaining that they've condemned their own selves with their fornication, going after false gods. Not heeding the word of God from the prophets but following the vain jangling from the false prophets telling the people that they were fine and judgment wasn't coming. That they were at peace with God. Even as they burned incense to idols and baked cakes to the "queen of heaven."

But chapter 18 begins with God sending Jeremiah to observe a potter, who is spinning the wheel to turn clay into a vessel. And, seeing the potter discard a bowl that didn't turn out right, to make another that would.

While many take the potter analogy and make it about us as individuals, because God does shape us to be fitted for His purpose, the primary application here, and in **Romans 9**, is about nations, specifically the physical nation of Israel. The descendants of Abraham.

*O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the Lord. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel. At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it*.

As Paul writes, nearly 8 centuries later;

*Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory*.

We see that the context remains the same. The destruction of the Jews serves God's purpose, that His wrath be manifest, but also His glory in those raised up in His mercy, the Gentiles.

God's judgment against Egypt and Pharaoh allowed His mercy to be seen in the children of Israel. His destruction of the northern kingdom, as a warning to Judah in the south. Judah's destruction by the Babylonians that Jeremiah is preaching will allow God to be glorified in their eventual return. The final destruction of the Jews in their rejection of Christ opens the door to the Gentiles to be graft in.

God uses the judgment against nations to bring about the glory of His mercy to those that believe. His wrath revealed from heaven allows His mercy and grace to be manifest in those He will be saved in His son.

teachings.title: God hates idols among His people
teachings.summary: Idol worship by those claiming His name, such as Catholics and Orthodox, provokes God's wrath and is a leading reason for the curses on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
It should go without saying that our God, Whose name is Jealous, and Who demands by His righteousness all the glory, hates Idolatry. He hates the veneration and worship of idols, *especially* by those claiming to be of His people. The Second Commandment is again hammered home here in the opening verse;

*Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.*

Those who call themselves by His name who bow before statues of stone, standing images and molten and graven idols, are what spark His wrath.

Catholicism and Orthodox Christianity, so called, the apostates who reject salvation by grace, and set up images to be served and bowed before in supplication, are the leading reason why Europe and America are suffering today. Why these curses and others spelled out by God throughout the Old Testament, are afflicting our land today.

When Asa became king and *he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made*, the Bible says he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord.

If we were to have a return to doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord, we who are His people would need to destroy every image and idol, from the blasphemy of St. Patrick's Cathedral, to every profane "crucifix," to every bathtub Mary in every Catholic yard, throughout the land.

teachings.title: God's if/then covenants with nations
teachings.summary: God's covenants with nations are conditional, judging nations by their works while He judges individuals by faith, and a nation that turns from wickedness can still be healed.
teachings.text:
We see near the end, after the triumphant singing and dancing unto the Lord, that the Israelites first begin to complain. And God makes a covenant with them as a nation, through Moses.

 *If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.*

All of God's covenants with the Hebrew are if/then. All come with responsibility of the people to hold to what God asks. This is the covenants with nations. With the people on this earth. God judges us as individuals spiritually by faith, but God judges nations on earth by their works.

This invitation to nations is still around today. It is how a godly nation that turns from its wicked ways becomes spared the evil God will do unto it.

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Idolatry and sodomites bring judgment
teachings.summary: Judah's idolatry and tolerance of sodomites provoked the Lord, and America is headed for the same judgment for false religion and sodomites in the land.
teachings.text:
Rehoboam, King over Judah, son of Solomon, reigned in Jerusalem 17 years, and under his leadership Judah too did evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking God to jealousy with their sins.

They also built up altars, groves and high places to worship strange gods. And they allowed sodomites in the land to commit the abominations of those nations the Lord had driven out to give the promised land to the children of Israel.

It is important to note that whenever people fall away from worshiping the true God and take up false gods and worship of idols, even under the guise of worshiping Him, it provokes the Lord. But allowing sodomites to exist and commit their filthy abominations is even more wicked and God punishes nations engaged in this behavior.

Judah was being protected for His name's sake, the coming of Christ and for the sake of that promise to David that was fulfilled in Jesus. But the Lord was wroth with the people and their king.

America is currently coasting on the blessings bestowed on our forefathers for their right worship of God, and the liberty found in Christ. And rapidly headed to judgment for idolatry and false religion, and the sodomites in the land.

The Lord took away the treasures in the Temple set by Solomon. All the gold, even the shields set in place by Rehoboam's father. The King sets a cheap imitation of the shields, made instead of brass. A humiliation.

Again, the rest of the story of Rehoboam is found in Chronicles.

teachings.title: The evil of sodomites given free reign
teachings.summary: The Gibeah outrage parallels Sodom to show the evil of a nation allowing sodomites free reign, which God's law calls an abomination worthy of death.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel*...and we know, men did what was right in their own eyes.

**Judges 19** begins another tale of the excesses and depravity that Israel fell into absent a Moses or Joshua. Relying on regional judges to come forth by God to deliver them from the results that came from the abominations they fell into.

This channel has covered the story told in **Judges 19-21** before, because it deals directly with the evil of allowing sodomites free reign in a nation.

The parallel to **Genesis 19** and the story of the destruction of Sodom is meant to drive home the point. Parallelism is God's way of signifying the importance of the message He is conveying.

A mob of baser fellows of the lewd sort, sons of Belial, Sodomites, surround a house in a city they are allowed free reign in, and there demand the master of the house deliver up a stranger, a man, that they may know him. These dogs burn with lust one for another, working that which is unseemly. Men with men, laying together. Abominations.

Worse they seek to force it by violence, in a mob. To a stranger, a sojourner. A Levite, of the priesthood.

None of the law or the things of God mattered to these reprobates, not retaining Him in their minds. Their conscience seared with a hot iron. Being twice-dead, fit to be burned.

**Leviticus 18:22**
*Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.*

**Leviticus 20:13**
*If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.*

**Deuteronomy 23:17**
*There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.*

**Romans 1:29-32**
*being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Abominations as capital crimes
teachings.summary: He teaches God's perfect law protects the innocent and that treating abominations as capital crimes is love, while teaching tolerance of sodomites is wicked.
teachings.text:
The Levite, upon receiving the remains of his raped and murdered concubine, defiled and slain by these dogs, took a knife and in his grief and anger, cut her corpse into twelve pieces and sent them as a message to all the coasts of Israel, telling the people of the great evil that had befallen him while in Benjamin. A deed not done or seen in the entire time the children of Israel had come up out of Egypt unto that day.

It was a national outrage. People saying to consider it, take advice and speak their minds. A viral story of outrage and abomination.

We know from elsewhere in Judges that the other tribes of Israel were themselves not following the way of the Lord. That every man was doing what seemed right in their own eyes. Some had fallen to false gods and Idolatry. Some had gone the way of the Canaanites whom they failed to cast out of their lands. Intermarrying. Doing that which is evil in the sight of God. And yet they couldn't imagine such evil.

The law of God is perfect. It exists that by following it to our best ability, we will prosper. It will be well with us. The blood of innocents won't be shed, the safety of our loved ones will be better assured. His blessings upon us. The inequity of the parents not visited on their children, generations not forced to deal with the consequences of the evil their fathers allowed.

Treating abominations as capital crimes is love for your people and love of God.

Feel good preaching to itchy ears, vain jangling leading silly women astray, teaching that capital punishment is no longer required in the New Testament is wicked. Teaching that God doesn't hate sodomites, that they need to be accepted as normal and tolerated, brought to repentance. That it's not our place to call for government, which wields the sword, to dispatch these sons of Belial...All of it is wicked and makes the people who accept it culpable for the evil done. Just as Benjamin was, for allowing their abominations to flourish.

teachings.title: No whore nor sodomite in Israel
teachings.summary: He refutes readings that make the sodomite a temple prostitute, teaching whores and sodomites were not to be tolerated nor their wages taken for vows.
teachings.text:
*There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.*

*Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore, or the price of a dog, into the house of the Lord thy God for any vow: for even both these are abomination unto the Lord thy God.*

There are some who try to use these verses to teach falsely that Sodomites are just male whores, or this is about temple prostitution or some other contrivance that allows the person making the argument to justify sodomites.

The first verse is clear. Whores and queers are not allowed among the children of Israel. A whorish daughter brings judgement on the people, and an abomination isn't fit to live.

The following verse takes the application to religious observance of taking a vow, where one would make a claim by sacrifice in front of God, ministered by the Levites with a sacrifice as we read in Leviticus and Numbers.

A whore isn't allowed to use their wages for this, including the sacrifice, and neither are the sodomites, which the Bible calls dogs repeatedly in scripture. It is an abomination to allow them to swear by the altar. To make it appear that God approves of their actions by taking the money. The prohibition is really against the priests, as there are other laws to deal with the harlot and the sodomite.

teachings.title: The land vomiteth out her inhabitants
teachings.summary: God judges nations for sexual perversion, idolatry and child sacrifice, and only turning from these sins heals the land.
teachings.text:
*Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you: And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.*

The judgment of God against nations is shown throughout the Bible. Here he tells us specifically the types of acts, sexual perversions, fornication, adultery, incest, bestiality, sodomy, that cause the land itself to visit the iniquity on the people, and spew them out. And it is these very acts that are promoted and encouraged on White, Western nations by the god of this world. The principalities, powers, and the rulers of the darkness of this world teach this spiritual wickedness.

These evils are pushed everywhere by Satan, who by his hatred of mankind seeks to damn us all. A ravening lion, seeking to devour us. But they are also weaponized by the enemy, to genocide a people. Again and again we see it in history, biblical and secular.

Child sacrifice, worshiping false gods, sodomy, sexual depravity. These are the causes of nations being destroyed.

It is only by turning from these sins that the land is healed and God repents of the evil He would visit upon a people.

teachings.title: Benjamin protected the sodomites
teachings.summary: Judges 19-21 shows God commanding war on Benjamin for protecting sodomites, a picture of our days when every man does what is right in his own eyes.
teachings.text:
The book of Judges is a difficult one, detailing the history between the settling of Israel under Joshua, and before the era of kings that begins with Saul. There are great heroes in the book, like Gideon and Sampson, but the key lesson throughout is that not everyone in the Bible behaves righteously. Many are wicked and sinful. The key to understanding is found in the often-repeated verse; *In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.*

That's the larger context. That even when the people turn to the Lord and do the right thing, it isn't always for the right reasons and many times they just do what they think is right in their own eyes.

All this to say the story told in Judges 19-21, of the sodomites protected within the tribe of Benjamin, and God's command to smite the tribe, He giving the others of Israel victory over them for their condoning and protecting these wicked sons of Belial, is very illustrative of the times we live in today, where people do what is right in their own eyes. Regardless of anything else; people were rightfully shocked and disgusted by the actions of the sodomites, and the willingness of Benjamin to fight to the death to protect those abominations. The fracture this war against a fellow tribe caused many divisions as we see. Much death. But the sodomites and most of their protectors were removed from the land.

teachings.title: Josiah removed the sodomites
teachings.summary: Good kings like Josiah tore down idols and removed the sodomites to win reprieve for the nation, so Christians must stand firmly against sodomites and evil.
teachings.text:
**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*if my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

We see throughout the Old Testament that the people of Israel, given every advantage by the blessings of God, His protection, the law, the ordinances, the faith in the Christ to come delivered by the Spirit unto the prophets, and yet they continually turn to Idolatry, building altars and groves, burning incense to the hosts of heaven, bowing down before strange gods, passing their children through the fire; killing them as a sacrifice to Baal, and tolerating the houses of the sodomites which do the abominations of the nations God has driven out of the promised land.

And God's wrath was kindled against the people. And He swore destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel and Judah.

But good kings came occasionally, and did what was right in the sight of the Lord, and when they did, they bought their people reprieve, as God repented for a time of the evil He was to do.

The Bible is clear in these accounts that not only did they tear down altars and kill the priests worshipping idols and burning incense to false gods (ahem RCC), but the sodomites were killed and removed from the land.

As we enter into June, it is important that we who call ourselves by His name, Christians, stand firmly opposed to the sodomites and all those who defy the judgment of God.

Like Josiah, who when he read the book of the law found in the Temple, rent his clothes and called for revival, being moved by the word of God, we must do the same. In season or out of season. Even if we are persecuted and attacked for it. We must call our evil when it is presented to us and have no fellowship with the sons of Belial.

teachings.title: Remove not the old landmark of the fatherless
teachings.summary: Stealing from the fatherless who have no one to plead for them brings God's vengeance, as with Ahab and Naboth, for their Redeemer is mighty.
teachings.text:
Solomon, as in the previous chapter, warns against moving landmarks. Here, in a very literal sense, taking land from the fatherless, stealing the inheritance of those who have no one to stand for their cause. This evil will be rewarded by God, He shall plead their cause, and it won't go well for you. Their Redeemer is mighty, indeed.

It is reminiscent of the story of Naboth the Jezreelite and his vineyard, told in **1 Kings 21**. Ahab king of Samaria, what was once the Northern Kingdom of Israel, desired the man's land. The queen, Jezebel, conspired to steal the land by false witnesses against Naboth, killing the poor man. Taking his inheritance.

Following the murder, God sends Elijah to pronounce judgment, prophesying that dogs will lick Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's, and that Jezebel will be likewise devoured.

God ensured that Ahab met his end at Jezreel, and the blood of Naboth was repaid in kind.

The perversion of justice is iniquity. The fatherless have an advocate in the Father. Never think those who we seem to have the upper hand over can be taken advantage of without recompense. Their Redeemer liveth.

teachings.title: Nations judged for shedding innocent blood
teachings.summary: A nation that refuses to punish those who shed innocent blood, whether by repealing capital punishment, funding abortion or bombing innocents, is guilty of that blood and God will judge it, so believers must stand against it.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 21** ramps up the commands of God in this, Moses giving of the law prior to entering the promised land. The land given as an inheritance to the children of Israel, if they maintain these rules to keep it. And right away God has let them know that the abominations of the Canaanites, their worship of idols and the shedding of innocent blood, were the cause of their own destruction. God judges nations for these things.

Here specifically, God gives provision for an unsolved murder along the wayside or in the wilderness. If a body be found, slain, and the elders of the nearest city do not know who did it, they were to take a heifer and offer a sacrifice, washing their hands of the matter. This of course is an image of Christ, as all the sacrifices pictured, the washing of the hands to show innocence before God for the bloodshed is just as Pontius Pilate did.

As the Lord declared to Noah; *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.*

**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalms 11:5**
*The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth.*

When a nation has refused to slay those who shed innocent blood, they are guilty of it. And God will repay. Be it repealing capital punishment, refusing to sentence a murderer to death, justifying or even funding abortions, bombing Innocents abroad, all these things bring judgment on a people, and the land will spew them out.

**Leviticus 18:28**
*That the land spew not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spewed out the nations that were before you.*

God requires of us that we stand against the shedding of innocent blood and seek His justice against those that do it.

teachings.title: Put away the guilt of innocent blood
teachings.summary: He teaches that God's law is founded on justice and avoiding innocent blood, so opposing the death penalty pities murderers and keeps the guilt on the nation.
teachings.text:
The foundation of God's law is justice, and the avoidance of shedding innocent blood. His mercy is extended to His people, who if they receive it means they must make provision for the innocent, and punish those who subvert the system.

In this case, the sanctuary cities for those who may by accident take the life of another are mentioned again, and God takes care to say to them to place them in central locations, easy to reach. And if they expand their borders by the blessings of God, to create more, that a man of vengeance, hot blooded, doesn't track down a person who committed manslaughter unwittingly, isn't killed on the way.

And if a murderer seeks sanctuary falsely, to be turned over to those seeking vengeance that they may die the death, because that is how the blood of the innocent victims are atoned.

*Thine eye shall not pity him, but thou shalt put away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with thee.*

Those that oppose the death penalty are taking pity on the murderers. Spillers of innocent blood. It prevents the guilt from being removed from the nation. It stymies God's justice.

God warns against cheating others of their inheritance by removing landmarks setting their property boundaries.

The same with false witnesses. That they should be punished in the manner of their accusations, that what could have happened to the person they perjured, happen to them. All to give an example to others not to do these evil things.

The deterrent is very important, as we will see going through the rest of the law.

teachings.title: Blood pollutes the land: the cities of refuge
teachings.summary: Bloodshed pollutes the land and brought judgment on Canaan and then Israel, so God's law of refuge cities minimized bloodshed.
teachings.text:
In **Numbers 35**, God gives the law of sanctuary cities and the judgments against murderers and the allowance for cases of manslaughter. Read through it and you really can appreciate how perfect God's law is.

With the granting of the land to the tribes of Israel, given by lot, the Levites who have no inheritance are to be given land within the tribes, cites and suburbs for living among them. To minister and serve.

And on top of that, given cities to serve as refuge for those that accidentally slay a man, that someone seeking revenge not slay them in return.

All to minimize the blood shed in the land, which cannot be cleansed. Multiple times in **Numbers**, the laws for cleansing those who were exposed to death or bloodshed. But the land itself cries out over bloodshed, as we saw in the murder of Abel;

**Genesis 4:8-10**
*And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?*

*And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground.*

It was this curse of Canaan, made by Noah when Ham had uncovered his father's nakedness, and so by the time of **Exodus**, the Canaanites land was polluted by the blood shed and offerings to idols. God's judgment upon them that they be dispossessed and slain to give the land to Israel.

But it was polluted again, even by the wickedness of the Israelites who turned to whoredoms and killed their own children to idols as the people there before them;

**Psalm 106:37-40**
*Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, And shed innocent blood, Even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, Whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: And the land was polluted with blood. Thus were they defiled with their own works, And went a whoring with their own inventions. Therefore was the wrath of the LORD kindled against his people, Insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance.*

And so the idea of having a city of refuge, where the innocent of murder could flee and live, so long as they were found to have done it by accident, until the death of the high priest.

That the revenger catching them outside the city was innocent of the blood. And that the murderer be put down upon the testimony of witnesses, their own blood being upon them. It's an elegant system that prevents the people from falling into tribal warfare, especially given the Levitical priests being among all the tribes.

teachings.title: Judgment on nations for innocent blood and idolatry
teachings.summary: God pours out judgment on nations that shed innocent blood and on apostate churches, like Rome and her daughters, that commit idolatry in His name.
teachings.text:
*For this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face, Because of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction. But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.*

*And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.*

Again and again we see God's judgment poured out on nations that shed innocent blood, child sacrifice as part of worshiping false gods being the worst example of this.

And in addition to this, the evil committed in His name, in His house. The offerings to false gods. The Idolatry. The burning of candles and incense to them. All in His holy name, this is abomination to God.

Apostate churches that engage in these abominations, who call themselves of Christ  but yet do these wicked acts, will not harken to instruction He has given, who reject His gospel for their own vain traditions; all of this brings judgement on a people. And because of it, our nations are being destroyed today.

Catholicism and its harlot daughters, false teachers and damnable heresies, idolatry and cannibalism (coming from the Canaanites), meat and drink sacrificed to idols, consuming "flesh and blood," all of it is abomination and His wrath abides on the people who allow it.

teachings.title: Abortion: passing children through the fire
teachings.summary: Abortion is today's child sacrifice to Molech and Mammon, and the women burdened by it should be reached with the gospel before their hearts are hardened.
teachings.text:
*And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord*.

Sacrifice of children to false gods was a common practice in every age and nation. We know that today, it is done through abortion. In Canaan, they sacrificed to Moloch. Today, it is often Mammon. It is horribly wicked. The bloody sacrifices to devils of their own children leads many to reprobation.

Women today have been pressured with unrelenting propaganda and social and economic incentives to use abortifacients as "birth control" and infanticide, while men have abandoned their proper role as a husband and father. Many, especially the women, carry this burden of sin and pain and are brokenhearted from it. It is important to try and reach them with the Gospel before they harden their hearts to sear their conscience.

teachings.title: God's commands for the king
teachings.summary: From the law of the king he teaches a ruler must be a brother, not multiply horses, wives or riches, since empire built on man's might is the seed of a nation's fall.
teachings.text:
Next are the admonitions against any future king that the people may seek (spoilers; they do!).

God lays out His commands for them. That it shall be one He chooses, not a stranger or foreign influence. Not someone who isn't of Israel, a brother. In modern practice, this would preclude putting a non-believer in charge.

He shall not multiply horses to himself, meaning not breed horses that he would eventually use for chariots of war. That he wouldn't create a cavalry for their army, which is both a false sense of security that would embolden the people to turn from trusting in God's mighty hand to defend them. But also invite the temptation of empire.

Empire and expansion by the nature of man's own might, rather than the will of God and the boundaries and habitations He provides, is often the beginning of the downfall of a nation. We are witness to it today. The empire is the seed of the destruction that takes down an empire. It is its own unsustainable end.

Neither were they to return the people to Egypt, both literally and figuratively. From a practical end, this was the murmurings of the Hebrews in the wilderness, that they had it better in bondage. Spiritually, it is returning to sin. To the bondage of the law vs the liberty of grace, and to backsliding into evil.

Of course, the king isn't to have multiple wives, primarily because they would cause "his heart to turn away," as we saw with Solomon. His wives led him to sin. To set up altars. The wisest man in history, and he couldn't resist this even with the clear teaching of God's word.

And of course God teaches against the storing up of riches, which Solomon did as well. The temptations of greed end kingdoms, and the united kingdom of Israel was divided and destroyed by these failures.

teachings.title: God's civil law still judges nations
teachings.summary: The civil punishments of Leviticus 20, unlike the ceremonial ordinances, are God's standard for judging nations and remain in effect today.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 20** begins laying out specific punishments for the violations of the civil laws given to Moses and Aaron by God, especially the paganism and the sexual immorality listed in the previous chapters. The sins of those whose lands the children of Israel were entering into, and the land the Lord freed them from, Egypt.

And as God frequently has stated in giving this law, the purpose was to separate the people unto God and away from the error, whoredoms and abominations of the other nations. To be holy because He is holy.

The law of God is perfect. His judgments are righteous. A just nation seeking after the Lord, who have the fear of God, would implement these strictures and punishments, that their nation not be judged, and the land that the Lord has granted them the habitations thereof wouldn't spew them out.

And so, as a practical matter, these things given by God, not to be confused with the ordinances and sacrifices that were done away with in the reformation of Christ, but rather are His law by which He judges nations. They are in full effect, even today. And His wrath is clearly upon those nations that don't follow His precepts.

teachings.title: Cut off for Molech and familiar spirits
teachings.summary: God commanded that those who gave children to Molech or went after mediums be cut off, showing His perfect will for a people seeking to be holy.
teachings.text:
And so, practically, physically, these laws give us insight to the perfect will of God for a people.

We start with a continuation of the following after false gods from chapter 19, where if a man offers his seed, that is his children, to Moloch, the false god of the Canaanites, he shall be cut off. Not allowed to defile the house of the Lord. Stoned to death, God's face turned from him. Reprobation. He is rejected and it is up to the people to do as God commanded and not to ignore his presence among them. This rejection is both physical and spiritual,  (I want to focus on the literal application as we go through the list of sins and punishment, tying in the spiritual application afterwards.)

Next he warns against those who go after mediums; those who have "familiar spirits," and after wizards, they too shall be cut off, the mediums and wizards stoned to death. Note these things are closely aligned with the false gods, because they are not only satanic but mean the person has no respect for the Lord, no fear of the living God, and has no faith in Him that saves, but rather seeks another god of their own invention. Reprobate concerning the faith, and physically cut off from the nation seeking to be holy. Sanctified.

*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

Again, separation by keeping God's statutes, that He may sanctify us. Something that Israel failed to do, and were cut off for when, after the longsuffering of God was over, Jesus had come in the flesh.

teachings.title: Restitution, not prisons: God's just law
teachings.summary: God's law of restitution for theft is just and perfect, and a nation living by His judgments would be better than man's criminal justice system.
teachings.text:
As we continue through the ordinances for the Levitical priesthood and sacrifices, we are also given more insight into the law, building on the fundamental of loving thy neighbor.

The sin of robbery by guile or by violence, by any dishonest means, was punished by restitution plus 5%, and a trespass offering. That's it.

Now as we saw yesterday, this required a confession of the wrong in order to share in the sacrifice for atonement, and obviously to restore the person who suffered loss.

God says this is just.

Man says we must create an entire criminal justice system with prisons and punishment, cops and robbers.

As we saw in Exodus 21, 22, there are more provisions for theft, and include instructions for those impenitent to or destitute to be given to servitude to repay. If they are caught breaking in and killed by the owner, there is no blood guilt. If there is harm done. Eye for an eye. Tooth for a tooth. Stripe for stripe.

God's law is perfect. It may not be able to save us, sinners as we all are. But for a nation to live by His perfect judgments, if they were to be followed, it would be a much better country. In our founding, much of the original laws came from the Old Testament. They are right and just.

**1 Timothy 1:8-11**
*But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

teachings.title: Babel: God scattered them into nations
teachings.summary: At Babel God confounded one-world man-made unity and scattered men into nations by kindred, and the genealogies mark the time from Adam to Christ.
teachings.text:
*And the whole earth was of one language, and the Lord said, Behold the people is one, and they have all one language...now nothing will be restrained of them, which they imagine to do.*

100 years after the flood, in the year of Peleg's birth (*for in his days was the earth divided*), the people imagined a vain thing. A tower to Heaven.

That they could work their way to Heaven and be like God.

*Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech*.

LORD God, the Father says "*let us go down*..."

And they scattered the people and confused their language. We are meant to be in nations. Nations by clan. By blood. Not one world government, full of vanity. Not even by a civic nationalism of paper and statutes that erases who we are, *making a name for ourselves lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.*

Nimrod gets a bad rap, having founded Babel and being a mighty man, a hunter before the LORD, it is assumed he's the impetus for the construction of the tower. Most of the assumption is based on his proximity, greatness, being a *gibboram* or mighty man, and his lineage forming the great cities listed in Genesis 10, Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

Some translate his name as "deserter," others "he rebelled" and take this to build an entire story around him, the tower, and great wickedness against God. Yet scripture doesn't give a negative accounting of him.

And then we are given the generations of Shem, leading to Terah father of Abraham and uncle to Lot.

And thus the genealogy of man after the flood is again given to establish where and when we are for the next phase of the story being told; the origins and chronology of the people whom God dealt with. Adam to Noah. Noah to Abram. And in like manner, the Gospels have similar genealogies, bringing us to Jesus Christ, that we have a lineage and time frame from Adam to Jesus earthly incarnation.

Many over look this as simply a history or chronological device, and try to extract much deeper meaning from it than is there, and often at the expense of believing it literally, especially the timing of years.

Also note, that the life spans of man are shrinking as we go from Shem to Abram. Approaching the 120yr avg God decided back in Genesis 6. Abraham would be 170 when he died. A shadow of the 900yrs most of the earlier patriarchs lived to.

teachings.title: The king's judgment and the powers that be
teachings.summary: Rulers are ordained of God to punish evil (Romans 13), not by divine right to do as they will, and a wicked king is an abomination like an unjust weight whom God will repay.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Proverbs 16**, we reach the proverbs of kings and the understanding that God behind their authority, in a similar way that He uses the wicked as a rod of His wrath or the chance of lots fall to His will (regardless of the roll of them, I believe. The power isn't in the roll, but in accepting His will in your heart).

The rule of God over government is a doctrine fully spelled out by Paul in Romans;

**Romans 13:1-5**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.*

But this isn't to say rulers are always correct and righteous, that there is a divine right of kings to do as they will. But their main function is to punish those that reject God's appointment, and His use of the anointed rulers to His purpose, whether good or evil.

The judgment of the king is a divine sentence. What they say, goes. Even as David refused to harm Saul, despite the evil Saul sought to do to him.

Just as the weights and balances used in trade are the Lord's. That's why, as we've previously read, an unjust weight is an abomination to Him. And so a king that commits wickedness is like an unjust weight, the ruler's iniquity is an abomination as well.

The Lord will repay.
