The righteous lips delight a king, and a wise man can pacify even a king's wrath. They hold the lives of men in their hands, and should they choose, they can easily take it. But the love of wisdom and true words, well spoken by the righteous man can pacify the ruler.

Finding favor with the king, is life and brings forth abundance as the spring rains.

In this context, we see the wisdom of vs 16: *How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver!*

When the wisdom and soft word of the righteous can curry favor and the mercy and blessings of the king, it is worth more than gold.

So we stick to the way of the Lord. Departing from evil. In the meekness and humility found in the fear of the Lord. Humble in spirit, rather than with the proud, even in their spoil. Because pride comes before destruction, and the spirit that God judges haughty will be brought low.

**Matthew 5:3-5**
*Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth*.

teachings.title: The powers that be are ordained of God
teachings.summary: God uses rulers good and bad to judge nations, so believers should not violently rebel but be subject, humble themselves, pray and get right with God.
teachings.text:
I would add that in addition to God using Satan, He uses David as the King to bring this upon the people.

God uses good rulers and bad rulers, the powers that be, the government, to enact judgment on the people for their sin, collectively. God judges nations on this earth.

**Romans 13:1-5**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake*.

Many Christians today hate this doctrine, and seek to riot in the daytime, to rebel against the government that is doing the Lord's bidding. That because a government is clearly satanic, we have a responsibility to violently react.

But the Bible teaches that we as believers have a responsibility to seek God's mercy and to come to Him asking for forgiveness. To do the things of God and turn unto Him. To get right.

It isn't for us to kick against the pricks.

That can be a hard lesson to swallow. Fear and pride can fight against the Spirit, but in the end, cannot prevail.

Better to trust in God and pray and offer thanksgiving and supplication. Win souls. Edify the brethren. Raise godly children.

*Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?*

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Render tribute: not paying taxes is sin
teachings.summary: Under Romans 13 refusing to pay taxes or obey the law on them is sin, and pastors who teach it are as harmful as false prophets.
teachings.text:
*For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.*

Not paying taxes and breaking the law regarding how they are administered, even to a church, is a sin.

You can pray they be lowered. You can be thankful God has made your church exempt. You can even take advantage of the various ways to structure your finances or your church's finances in a way that best serves to maintain the Spirit of the law and service to the Gospel.

But a so-called pastor in a living room church, refusing to obey the law and encouraging others to do the same almost always is a false prophet and as damaging to the cause of Christ as a false prophet who abuses the system to create a 501c3 in order to mislead people, too.

They are the same.

teachings.title: Romans 13: living in godly subjection
teachings.summary: Believers are to submit to the authorities God ordains, obeying God rather than man only where they conflict, and trust God, for godly subjection is how God changes who rules over us.
teachings.text:
Romans 13 continues the theme of how saved Christians are to behave. It begins telling us God's view of earthly authority. Parents, bosses, civic leaders, law enforcement, all authorities under God, wicked and cruel or righteous and kind, to serve His will.

Of course we are to follow the higher law of God when earthly authority contradicts it. We are to obey God rather than man, but *if at all possible to live peaceably with all men*.

Many of us bristle at this. It requires our subjection and faith that God will protect and deliver us. Paying custom and tribute to people we know are wicked, stupid, foolish, deceitful is a hard thing to swallow. Not going into reactionary spirals. Not acting from fear. Honoring God by honoring those he's placed in authority over you. Starting with parents for children, husbands for wives, bosses for husbands.

When authority places you in conflict with God, meekly and in His name refuse, but attempt to offer a solution, even one that may harm your interests short term, that you may render what is acceptable to God and in doing so be rewarded long term.

This is so hard in our current year. But if it's fake and gay, can't be voted out, can't be fed posted, and God is with you anyways, what more can we do but live in Godly subjection? At worse be persecuted for His sake and be rewarded here and for eternity. At best be an example as to how God delivers His sons and daughters from tribulation so that others may believe, and in doing so change the nature of the people, turning them towards God. This is how the Bible teaches us we change who rules over us to a more benevolent or tolerable authority. It's how we win.

Hard lesson in faith.

teachings.title: No freedom of religion in the Kingdom
teachings.summary: Conversion comes by the word and never the sword, so the Baptist distinctive of freedom from state religion is right, churches should be local, independent and Christ led, and a godly people should not allow false religions to be practiced.
teachings.text:
There is no "freedom of religion" in the Kingdom of Heaven. There is a right to individuals to choose not to believe. No one can force conversion by the sword, only by the word. But the allowance and practice of false religions should never be allowed by a Christian people.

The Baptist Distinctive regarding freedom from state religion is good, and right. A secular denomination with political power to force conversions will always create false gospels and result in persecution of believers. Churches should be local and independent, Christ led. Not top-down controlled by men.

A nation of believers should enforce this rule, destroying cults that worship other gods and lead others to apostasy. In my opinion.

But to have such a thing requires a godly people. The blessings of liberty are only bestowed on a nation when a large enough portion are at liberty in Christ.

Idolatrous sects, pagans, Jews, satanic cults, perverse groups who seek after other gods, rejecting the God of our fathers, should never have been given the freedom to spread their abominations.

There was a time when our forefathers understood that. The same people who wrote and adopted the Bill of Rights did not allow antichrist religions. Or at least tried not to. They blew it, in the end. And our people turned from God and now we suffer as a nation for it, making the point moot.

But this will be enforced in the Millennium. Amen.

teachings.title: There is no liberty outside of Christ
teachings.summary: True liberty comes only from salvation in Christ, not from any constitution, and only God blesses a nation through those who keep the faith.
teachings.text:
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage*.

This 4th of July, Independence Day, remember that the blessings of liberty come from the liberty found in Christ. There is no liberty outside of Christ.

It isn't an abstraction that can be grasped and measured. It isn't a concept to be understood and maintained in a secular setting. It has no meaning without the Gospel, the beautiful law of Liberty.

*But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.*

America secured the blessings of liberty through the faith of the founding stock. Not their masters. Not their king, not in the men that replaced him. Not in their documents. It isn't to be found in the Constitution. No parchment has or can grant liberty, or the blessings that come from it. Only salvation by grace through faith in Christ Jesus can.

And only God may bless those who maintain the faith and live it out, regardless of where or when.

And those blessings that abound to the faithful can continue and grow to the benefit of everyone in their nation, regardless of their faith. But the only way to secure those blessings is in the Lord;

*Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

teachings.title: Romans 13: Paul obeyed authority in faith
teachings.summary: Notes that Paul wrote Romans 13 under Roman rule and obeyed authority unless it conflicted with God. Points to Paul staying in the Philippian jail to win the jailer, who is told only to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ.
teachings.text:
FFS the Romans were in charge and persecuting Christians when he wrote that. They had Paul under house arrest, chained to a guard. 

Paul trusted God and obeyed authority, in faith.

Paul could have escaped the Philippian jail after the divine earthquake, but he stayed to get the jailer saved in Acts 16:25-31

*25 And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

26 And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.

27 And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

29 Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,

30 And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

31 And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

Paul obeyed authority to the glory of God. 

Note he doesn't say "repent of your sins and be saved" or "get baptized" or "go to church" or "do sacraments" or any other work. Just believe. Call on the name of the Lord.

teachings.title: God is no respecter of persons
teachings.summary: Jewish ethnic supremacy is wicked since God is no respecter of persons; He judges individuals by faith and nations by works and always offered His blessing to any who trusted Him.
teachings.text:
*The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men. From the place of his habitation he looketh upon all the inhabitants of the earth. He fashioneth their hearts alike; he considereth all their works.*

We are all the same in His eyes. We are all guilty before Him, convicted in sin. All are in need of a savior.

The modern form of Jewish ethnic supremacy, a concept that as God's chosen people, it is because of their own qualities and holiness, is wicked. God is not a respecter of persons.

He judges individuals by faith and nations by works. And the offer to give His blessings to any king who chose to place their trust in Him, rather than strength of horses and size of armies, was always extended.

Nineveh was spared by their faith, believing the reluctant prophet Jonah. King Nebuchadnezzar's humbling 7 years in the wilderness struck with madness, led to him proclaiming the truth of God to the world. The Queen of the South came to Solomon in order to understand the truth of God.

*Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy; To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.* Whosoever will come, He shall deliver.

And so we sing.

*Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield. For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.*

Amen!

teachings.title: Why do the heathen rage
teachings.summary: Psalm 2 prophesies the rulers' vain rebellion against God's anointed, whom God raised up and set as King over the nations, warning rulers to kiss the Son and trust in Him.
teachings.text:
Why do the heathen rage? Why do people think they can go against God? Kings and rulers, presidents and prime ministers, popes and priests, all seek to be freed from the ways of the Lord, to do what they will.

Especially the religious and political leaders in the time of Jesus.

**Acts 4:27**
*For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together*.

They believed if they killed the Son, they would break the bands, Their bonds, and be free of God.

Jesus addressed this in a parable, about a Lord who planted a vineyard and lent it out to husbandmen to dress and keep it. And when the Lord sent servants to gather the harvest, the stewards beat and killed them. So finally, the Lord sends his son;

**Matthew 21:38**
*But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance*.

David prophetically writes of this here in **Psalm 2**.

But, it is folly. The Lord holds them in derision. He laughs at their vain efforts, because Christ, His anointed, rose again.

He set His Son upon Zion, and upon the throne.

**Acts 13:32–33**
*And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.*

Jesus' inheritance are all the nations of the world, and possession of the uttermost parts of the world. And as Lord of lords and King of kings, He will rule them.

**Revelation 2:26–27**
*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.*

This prophetic Psalm gives warning to the rulers of this world, reminding them of their place. That they serve at the pleasure of the Lord, and He will deliver vengeance.

It's an amazing and consistent message, across the entire Bible; The Christ is God's anointed, and Jesus is the Christ. All who believe on Christ Jesus shall be saved. His grace and mercy giving us the chance to serve Him in righteousness.

*Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

Amen

teachings.title: They that forsake the law praise the wicked
teachings.summary: Law-haters who use grace to excuse sin go on to praise the wicked, sodomites and rioters, while believers keep the law, abhor evil and honour the powers that be.
teachings.text:
What follows, from verse 3 though 28, is a litany of sayings that contrast the wicked, the rich without understanding, the haters of the law, the violent and bloody man, with the faithful, upright, keepers of the law. The prince of understanding, the righteous man, these see their fortunes and their reputation in increase, while their counterparts are undone by their sin.

We see that a poor man who helps oppress the poor is a threat to all, and also self-destructive.

That those who forsake the law will praise the wicked, but this that keep the law will contend with them. Those law-haters out there, that make grace an opportunity to justify their sin, will inevitably go after the praise of the wicked. We see it all the time. It begins with excusing themselves from God's precepts, and extends to then justifying sodomites and degenerates. Female led churches with rainbow flags, glorifying rioting and rebellion, and teaching abominations.

Because evil men understand not judgment, they are perverse and so oppose any mention of what God says, to chase after their own lusts. "God wouldn't want the death penalty!" or "A loving God wouldn't send anyone to Hell!" Those that seek the Lord and in all our ways acknowledge Him, understand the need for love being without dissimulation. Why we must abhor that which is evil.

We are reminded again it is better to be poor and walking in God's ways, than to be rich and wicked.

A wise son keeps the law and is a joy to his parents, but the riotous and rebellious son is a shame to his father.

**Romans 13:13**-**14**
*Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying.* *But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.*

As Christians, we are to give honor, tribute and custom to whom it is due. To obey the higher authority and the powers that be. Not seek cause for lawlessness and giving the wicked praise because they cause the righteous to go astray unto evil.

teachings.title: Taking a dog by the ears
teachings.summary: Meddling in others' fights, from church disputes to online drama, is folly, and likewise a godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in their wars, as Jehoshaphat was rebuked for helping Ahab.
teachings.text:
The last section of **Proverbs 26** deals with strife, and those that cause it with their lying tongue.

*He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears*.

Getting involved in other people's fights, whether it's taking up a cause between two parties in your church, between neighbors, or total strangers, is a foolish thing to do. The warning here leans into the uncontrollable danger, likening it to a dog turning and rending you.

But it also applies to chatroom drama and Facebook fights. It happens online all the time, where the physical stakes are low, and the busybody tendencies are not inhibited by potential violence.

Stay out of contentions that don't involve you. If we are to bless our own enemies and turn the other cheek, then what business is it of ours to join in another's vengeance?

And, while it is blessed to be a peacemaker, it isn't arrived at by stepping in between brawlers or meddling in their strife.

Better to counsel with soft words to the parties separately, than join in as a third member of an ongoing fight. You really don't want to be the reason two warring factions unite out of spite to go after you for your meddling.

This should be applied in context to ruling a kingdom as well. When Jehosaphat, King of the Southern Kingdom of Judah joined the wicked Ahab of Israel in his war with Syria, we see in **2 Chronicles 19**; *Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord.*

A godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in war against their enemies. And Christians shouldn't cheer when their leaders yoke with unbelieving countries to make war.

If two nations of those who hate God choose to go to war, you can pray for God's will to be done, or that His judgement brings peace. You can be indifferent to the outcome, and leave it to God. But don't meddle in their strife, even by egging it on.

teachings.title: The Lord pondereth the hearts
teachings.summary: God ordains rulers and directs the king's heart, and He judges the spirit behind men's deeds, valuing mercy and judgment over sacrifice, so the sacrifice of the wicked is abomination.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 21** adds to the sayings of the king, first hand advice of Solomon to his heir, that God is the master and commander of the ship of state, as He sets the heart of the king to His own devices.

Just as the Lord said of Pharaoh;

**Romans 9:17**
*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

And the government is on the shoulders of whom its given;

**Romans 13:1**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

What a humbling saying for a young prince to hear. For good or ill, God's anointed is ordained to power in His will and to the Almighty Lord's purpose.

*Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.* The spirit behind what a man does, this is what God judges. The things we do in sin aren't only those things that no good led to, fornication, iniquity, theft, deceit, covetousness...those aren't the only ways we sin and fall short. Often we can do the right things for the wrong reasons. God knows our hearts.

That's why, especially for a prince, to do justice and judgment, with fairness and right spirit, means more to God than sacrifice. As Jesus says to the Pharisees;

**Matthew 9:13**
*But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance*.

This, quoting **Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

This leads to a theme of the heart of the wicked. Their tendencies and traits.

The high look and proud heart of the wicked, their plans and schemes, this is sin. Diligence has a reward, haste leads to want.

Lying for wealth is a vanity, the wise king says, and it is passed back and forth between thieves, those that seek death and not life. There is no honor among thieves. Their robberies end in death. They are destroyed by their ways. They refuse judgment. Everything they seek to gain is motivated by greed and covetousness. Their way is froward and strange. But for the pure, those seeking to walk on God's path, their work is right.

The wicked desires evil. They do not love even their neighbors, violating even the second great command.

**Matthew 22:37-39**
*Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.*

In the end, God will overthrow the wicked for their wickedness. The wicked ignore the cries of the poor, and so God will not hear the wicked's cry.

Their love of pleasure results in poverty, that lack of impulse control. High time preference. This will ruin a man led by his own desires. A foolish man spends all he has.

Scorners are proud and haughty, their wrath comes from their pride. Overreacting to slights. Their pride insulted.

The lazy are their own destruction, the slothful kills themselves by their lack of labor. Their end is hunger. They shall always want.

The covetous, often the same foolish, lazy, proud and unjust fool, the robber, he who hates his neighbor, they are consumed by their greed all day long.

God promises the false witness will perish, and the wicked is set in their ways.

Tying this thread all back together to the beginning, we are given the understanding God judges hearts, the spirit of the man, and He values mercy and judgement over sacrifice, we see then the truth; *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?*

teachings.title: The Lord hath made all things for himself
teachings.summary: God judges the spirit behind men's deeds and uses even the wicked, like Assyria, for His purposes, so we should commit our works to Him and walk in the fear of the Lord, which brings wisdom and makes even our enemies be at peace with us.
teachings.text:
Following the opening verse, we get a quick succession of proverbs that highlight the way of the Lord, and insight to His understanding.

The Lord judges the ways of a man by the spirit behind what we do. Men may justify every deed and word, but it is the intent and heart behind them that God cares about. A man can do good for bad reasons, he can do evil with good intentions. We do things in ignorance, we do things willfully, and so God judges righteous judgement, as only He can.

And so, to ensure we are walking in His ways, we are encouraged to commit our works to the Lord and our thoughts will be established. The spirit behind our deeds will be His, rather than our vain rationalizations.

The Lord has made all creation, everything that is, is His. Even the wicked who do evil serve a purpose for the Lord. Consider Assyria;

**Isaiah 10:1-6**
*Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless! And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory? Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.*

The destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel by the heathen empire was done by the wicked. Assyria is described as the rod of God's anger. Again the sovereignty and judgment of the Lord results in all things being for His purpose. Not determinism, but utility of the ultimate authority, towards His ends.

The proud of heart are an abomination to the Lord, even when they join forces against Him. I think of the armies Satan deceives into attacking Jesus and the camp of the saints at the end of the Millennial Kingdom, appealing to their pride. They unite for the battle of Gog and Magog, and are instantly destroyed, punished for their pride.

**Revelation 20:7-9**
*And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.*

As we have been instructed over and over again, fear of the Lord brings understanding and wisdom, wisdom brings mercy and love of truth, and these in practice purge iniquity and injustice from men.

By heeding the wisdom of the Lord, by seeking and walking in His paths, by acknowledging Him in all our ways, we please the Lord and rather than the destruction of the prideful and the visiting of evil, He will even make our enemies be at peace with us.

In **Genesis 26:28-29**, Isaac prospered and lived righteously, causing his chief enemy, King Abimelech, to come to him seeking a covenant of peace, acknowledging that God was with him.

This is most evident in the cycle of Judges.

**Judges 2:14-19**
*And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed. Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.*

teachings.title: He that hath mercy on the poor
teachings.summary: Remembering the poor is done unto Christ and lent to the Lord, and since righteousness exalteth a nation we should win souls so it becomes a nation of Christians, not Christian nationalism.
teachings.text:
Remember the poor. Do not despise them, as we are poor in spirit and God gave to us abundantly. As Jesus said;

**Matthew 25:35-40**
*For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.*

And the promises of God to repay, that when we give to the poor we lend to the Lord.

**Psalms 41:1**
*Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.*

And again, in verse 32 we see the gospel in **Proverbs**, the righteous has hope in our death. That blessed hope of eternal life in Christ Jesus. This is wisdom, to hear and believe the truth of God's mercy and grace, by the imputed righteousness of Christ.

Because righteousness exalteth a nation and sin is a reproach to any people, we should strive to win souls, instruct wisdom, have standards, that our nation would be blessed by our righteousness in Christ. Not Christian nationalism but a nation of Christians.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: Women rule over them: men abdicating authority
teachings.summary: God's order is for men to rule in the family and the nation, to be ruled by women is a shame and a curse, and when women usurp authority it is first the fault of men abdicating it, as Adam did.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 3:12**
*As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.*

While each of us are given some dominion over something in our lives, male or female, the order of things as given by God is for men to rule in positions of power in the family and the nation. To be ruled by women is a shame and a curse.

This extends to the household as much as it does to government.

To the extent that women may usurp the authority of men, it is always the fault of men for abdicating their authority first.

Adam, knowing the word of God forbidding the fruit of the tree in the midst of the garden, took it and ate it to please Eve.

When men rule poorly, weakly or without love for their subjects, cruel and ungodly, the results can end poorly for all concerned.

Judah is about to experience 6 years of pain for the sin brought about by their kings' poor choices. Just as America is threatened with the same for ours.

teachings.title: The commandments are still in force
teachings.summary: He refutes professing Christians who use the end of ceremonial laws to excuse sodomy and adultery, teaching that God's moral commandments still stand.
teachings.text:
*Thou shalt not kill.*

*Neither shalt thou commit adultery.*

*Neither shalt thou steal.*

*Neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour.*

*Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbour's house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is thy neighbour's*

The 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th commandments as God gave them, are simple to understand, and as eternally relevant as the first five.

There are some professing Christians today who claim the civil laws of God and His commandments given Moses, are no longer in force. They point to the ceremonial laws and carnal ordinances of the Levitical priesthood that were done away with in Christ, and apply it to things like sodomy and adultery. Saying that these things are allowed in the New Testament. That the death penalty has been done away with. That God now loves abominations. "If the dietary laws aren't in effect, if you can eat pork and shrimp, then there's nothing wrong with being a Sodomite!"

Of course, these same people would not claim that murder, cheating on a spouse, stealing, perjuring or coveting the things of others are now ok.

They simply want to call evil good and good evil. They want to pick and choose, and not knowing scripture or hoping those they seek to mislead don't, they make these ridiculous claims.

But we know better.

*Ye shall observe to do therefore as the Lord your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land which ye shall possess.*

teachings.title: Idolatry and reprobate nations
teachings.summary: Nations that turn to idolatry behave as Romans 1 describes and are given over to God's judgment, as the Canaanites and Israel were, and Catholic and Orthodox idolatry has brought that same judgment on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
*Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord thy God hath forbidden thee. For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord thy God, to provoke him to anger: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed. And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.*

This prohibition against Idolatry was not only to Israel. The nations being driven out before them had fallen to Idolatry, forgotten the Lord God that brought them out of Noah and his sons. They committed abominations. They behaved as **Romans 1**:18-**25** describes; reprobate.

*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

Moses tells them that they will suffer the same judgment as a nation if they turn to idols. That they will be destroyed, made desolate, driven from their homeland, scattered. This is God's judgment on all nations that turn from Him to serve idols, and even more so those nations claiming to be called His.

This same judgment that destroyed the Canaanites, ultimately destroyed the Israelites, who were rejected of God. Reprobate silver. Given up and given over to their vain imaginations. And this same judgment exists today.

Roman Catholicism and Orthodoxy especially, have turned entire nations to idolatry, and in doing so, brought the judgment of God upon them. This is why Europe was overrun with Muslims in the past, and why it is happening again today. And in other Christian nations that have allowed altars to idols to flourish are seeing the same judgment, especially America.

More than Sodomites, more than antichrist Jews, people claiming to be Christian yet bowing and praying to idols, worshiping the created more than the Creator, are the reason for our current state.

We are overrun with the fruits of a Reprobate mind; sodomy and abominations. We are being ethnically cleansed. Our children barren and filled with all unrighteousness. And it first starts with idolatry. This is the primary lesson of the Reprobate Doctrine.

teachings.title: Promises to Lot and Esau, and nations judged
teachings.summary: God gave land to Lot and Esau too, yet destroyed those nations for wickedness, so modern Jews have no claim, for God gives and takes away the bounds of nations.
teachings.text:
Here in **Deuteronomy 2**, Moses continues his retelling of the time in the wilderness, the 40 years recounted in part in the **Book of Numbers**. There are some perspective changes and details added that broaden the underlying history, and containing details that flesh out the story.

A few things that stand out to me in this reading; the promises of land to Lot and Edom, and the nature of the giants that were in many of these lands.

Modern "Jews" and their Zionist pets will make quite a big deal about the conditional covenant made in the wilderness to deliver the land to Israel, which had been promised to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ. A promise repeated to Issac and Jacob. They claim ownership as the nation of Israel (by deception, but none the less) based off this idea that they are the inheritors. But the promises to Lot and Esau were to the nations they spawned, by the blessings of God, and yet those nations were destroyed in time, and the land taken as spoil, after the wickedness of the people. The same as Israel. The same as the remnant in Judah. God judges nations on this earth and their bounds and habitations are His to give and take away.

teachings.title: Miriam's sedition against the man of God
teachings.summary: Numbers 12 is about sedition against the man God placed over His people, not about mixed marriage, though scripture still warns against marrying strangers.
teachings.text:
So, we are here in **Numbers** chapter 12, and we have a story of the brother and sister of Moses, Aaron and Miriam, and their sedition against Moses because of his marriage to an outlandish woman, an Ethiopian.

Claiming they were on par with Moses, having had the Spirit of the Lord upon them and having then preached His word through them, they presumed to speak with authority over the appointed man of God.

Moses in his meekness didn't speak against them, but the Lord in His anger did, saying that His inspiration to prophecy given men in visions and dreams wasn't the same thing as His relationship with Moses which was direct and personal, speaking mouth to mouth. Not in "dark speeches," or dark sayings as parables and metaphors used to teach doctrine are called in the New Testament. But directly. Frankly. In person. God asks why they are not afraid to speak out against Moses given that obvious position of favor and authority that had been granted him.

And His wrath was kindled, and Miriam became leprous, skin as white as snow. Aaron seeing this begged for forgiveness to Moses, who then intercedes on Miriam's behalf. But the Lord, to show Miriam and others who might rise in sedition a lesson, has her put without the camp for 7 days of shame.

This chapter has been used to justify or argue something about mixed marriages with other nations, races, kindred, religion...to justify miscegenation, and to condemn those who oppose taking a stranger as a spouse. The "Ethiopian wife" and the "white as snow" punishment of Miriam, has added to this debate.

But it's not what the chapter is about.

It is literally about sedition and setting yourself up as better than or worthier than the man of God that He has placed over you in His hierarchy.

That even if you disagree with their own life choices and resent them for whatever reason, you still must respect God's choice, giving honor to those who should be honored. Tribute to those due tribute.

**1 Samuel 15:23**
*For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.*

The reason behind their rebellion is incidental. They used a flaw in Moses to seek to undermine him. That's the essence of the story. If that's who God puts in place of power, given the spirit of leadership over the people, then that's who God chose. Render honor to them, and fear the Lord.

It doesn't change the fact that there are several prohibitions and warnings against taking outlandish women as wives. That taking a stranger for a wife leads to children who fall away from the faith of their fathers and chase idols. It is a punishment on a nation to be bred out of existence, and it begins by the acceptance of mixed marriage. It was especially true in the idea that Israel was a means of getting from Abraham to David to Christ Jesus. And it remains true in a spiritual sense today, and being unequally yoked, and the judgment against nations being ethnically erased still exists, and will unto the day of redemption.

God sets the boundaries and habitations thereof. The nations will rejoice in that day. And we will be one people in the resurrection. Until then, it isn't prudent to be accepting culturally of miscegenation.

teachings.title: Mary as co-redeemer and the cult of the queen
teachings.summary: Rome makes Mary a co-redeemer and mediatrix, no different from the Jews in Egypt who credited the queen of heaven, and such idolatry brings nations to destruction.
teachings.text:
Tradition dictates that Mary is part of the monarchy of heaven, soliciting grace and mercy from the Lord on behalf of sinners, and covering sin by distributing from her "Treasury of Merit." She becomes a "co-redeemer" with Christ in His suffering on the cross, and is now a "co-mediator" alongside Him in heaven—essentially an alternative avenue of access to God. They blasphemously replace the Holy Spirit and His role in bestowing aid and comfort to believers with Mary. In effect, she becomes an additional member of the Trinity. The Mother of God. The Queen of Heaven. Mediatrix. And they pray to her for salvation.

There's very little difference in this and the attitudes of the Jews in Egypt, who credited their worship of the "queen of heaven" for their prosperity, and their halfhearted turn towards the true and living God as the cause for their calamity.

And so God vows to destroy them, and does.

Again, I have posted about this before but it bears repeating; It is the people calling themselves by His name who worship idols and profane God that leads to a nation's destruction. The West is currently paying the price for the return of the cult of the queen.

teachings.title: Jeremiah teaches us to face a nation's judgment
teachings.summary: Jeremiah and Lamentations prepare believers to be at peace when judgment falls on their nation, trusting God's perfect will and His promised deliverance.
teachings.text:
Now we're there in chapter 14 of Jeremiah and we see a continuation of what has become the pattern over the past few chapters, that Jeremiah is beseeching the Lord for mercy for his people while the Lord preaches through Jeremiah to them about their sin. And especially the judgment that has come upon them.

As it goes, we see Jeremiah becoming more desperate in pleading the case for the children of Israel. And we see God has hardened His heart against them. He is promising that they shall die by famine and by sword and be carried away captive into a strange land. God's mind is set upon this judgment and His wrath is upon them.

In chapter 14, we see Jeremiah begging not to do this to the people who call themselves by his name, Who are his people. And God says don't even bother praying for them. They can't make burnt offerings or fast enough for Him to repent. Reprobate, silver shellman call them because the Lord has given up on them.

Again, the parallels to today are striking. And again, we should remind ourselves that in all times and places there have been Jeremiah's. And there have been people who have done wickedly and received the just wrath of God.

Part of the  reason for the book of Jeremiah and lamentations that follow is to help set us in the right frame of mind and understanding when tribulation comes to our nations. When the wickedness of our people leads us to destruction. That we can be at peace with it even as we preach hard against it. Hoping that our people turn back to the Lord.

Much like Job and understanding how God deals with us as individuals, Even we who are righteous in His name.

But also like Job. It is easy to empathize and feel the emotion as they go through their trials and tribulations. The frustration of it. But it's humbling to understand that God's will is not our will. And God's point of view is outside of time and perfect while we see through a glass darkly. Our faith should be bolstered by reading this because we know how it turned out in the end. And we know how Israel was delivered by Christ and the resurrection promised in the scriptures by a God who cannot lie. And so we should take comfort in that as the people who call ourselves by His name. As we await a better country.

teachings.title: God gives many chances, then judgment
teachings.summary: God warns nations, backsliders and the lost again and again, but after rote religion and wickedness continue, His judgment comes and He forbids intercession.
teachings.text:
The preaching of the word of God continues, Jeremiah prophesying in the Spirit that God is casting His judgment upon a wicked and perverse generation of Judah.

As He frequently does, the Lord, being long-suffering and full of mercy and grace, extends His hand first. Saying; *Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.*

Because the judgment of nations is done on this earth. And the wickedness of those who are His people will be met with the rod of correction and reproof.

We serve the living God and as His sons, the spiritual seed of Abraham, we too face this judgment for our inequity and the inequity of the people.

But, because of His love, grace is always available to those sons who repent. The prodigal who returns home. The nation where the people who call themselves by His name turn back towards Him, God promises to heal.

God instructs Jeremiah to preach at the door of the temple, to those in Judah entering in for sacrifice and burnt offerings, but who outside the temple blaspheme God. Serving other gods. Committing wickedness; they
*steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not*, and yet out of habit and vain faith they return to His temple to do the performative religious acts, that do not save them.

*Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.*

This is the scripture Jesus preaches during His scourging of the moneychangers in the Temple;

**Matthew 21:13**
*And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.*

It's the same spirit that gripped the Pharisees, rote practices of ordinances but nothing given to the weightier matters of the law;

**Matthew 23:23**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone*

God says He has spoken to them, warning them, calling out to repent and they didn't hear. *They answered not.*

When God says this, He obviously means it literally, that through the prophets He has instructed His people and warned them, but more; He had recently allowed the entire Northern Kingdom, and the 10 tribes therein, to be destroyed and scattered by the Assyrians, for just such behavior. The whole seed of Ephraim, being the most prominent tribe of Israel, represents those northern 10 tribes. He reminds them "I have cast out all of thy brethren."

God gives His people chances. Repeatedly. He gives unsaved people multiple chances as well. The Spirit moving to rebuke the world that they may come to believe. But eventually, be it judgment upon a nation that is destroyed, judgment against a backslidden believer where they are rebuked and eventually called home if they don't respond, or to the unbelievers who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, and are made reprobate. God gives us multiple chances and warnings to repent towards Him and His mercies.

God says to Jeremiah, don't even bother praying for intercession. He is done with these people. This is on them, their last chance.

teachings.title: The covenant kept in Christ, not in the Jews
teachings.summary: Leviticus 26's remedy of confession is fulfilled in Christ, and God's Israel is believers circumcised in heart, while unbelieving Jews remain under the curse.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 26** is one of the many times God reiterates the warning to Israel, that if they don't keep the conditions of the covenant God has made with them, he will curse them 7-fold, remove them from the land and set their enemies up over them.

This held specific meaning to the Hebrews in the wilderness, entering into Canaan, but it is true of all people who call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

The curse against His people comes with a remedy. Because the Lord is a forgiving and merciful God.

*If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me; And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.*

(Note the physical circumcision availa them nothing. It is the circumcision of the heart, made without hands, in Christ Jesus;

*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ*.
...
*But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*)

This covenant is and always has been kept in Christ. It was to Abraham's seed, who is Jesus, and those blessings fall on those adopted into the promise by faith in Him. Those calling themselves Jews today *could* repent to be partakers of the promise, but note that they'd have to admit not only that they forsook God and didn't walk in His statutes, rejecting Christ, and deserved their punishments, but they'd have to also testify that God has walked contrary to them, and that His judgment was right.

In the various captivities and tribulations of the OT Israelites, this repentance led to their being restored. But modern Jews, so-called, maintain in their being scattered, in their being cursed, in their being kept from peace in the land, they keep the fiction that they remain God's chosen people. That they aren't being cursed for their unbelief, but that it is we who believe, those circumcised of the heart, who afflict them unjustly.

*And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.*

This is seen in the ADL and the cries of "antisemitism," seeing swastikas and threats of genocide in construction markings and preaching from the Bible. The wicked flee where none pursue. They are faint of heart, as the Lord promises.

Talmudic rabbinical Judaism shows that they despise God's statutes and abhor His judgements, so that they do not keep His commandments but instead find loopholes and rationalizations in the vain traditions of men, doctrines they invented taught as commandments of God.

His tabernacle is not set in their midst, who is Jesus. They are contrary to all men. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost.

God's people, Israel, has always been a nation of believers who, by faith, carry the circumcision of the heart. Today it is believing Christians, and our nations are blessed by the few within it who keep the word of God, and cursed when we who call ourselves by His name reject His judgement.

teachings.title: Woe to them that join house to house
teachings.summary: God's jubilee law forbade usury and the hoarding of land, a fair system neither capitalist nor communist that kept families and tribes intact and still shows how to live.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 5:8**
*Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!*

God hates unfair dealings, taking advantage of others for profit, especially in their poverty. Unjust weights and measures. Mistreatment of servants. Usury among His people and the accumulation of property and capital, to the exclusion of others.

Basically, Capitalism.

But that is not to say He endorsed Communism, either. But fair and righteous trade and checks on over accumulation of wealth, or subjugation of His people. Productive enterprise and free markets (little f, little m), were the way He provided.

This system was fair and just and kept in remembrance of God being who we rely on, who provides for all. Rich or poor, servant or free.

The right of return to their own place, the inheritance they claim, enabled the genealogies to be recorded, and kept the tribes separated as He had ordained through the lots when it was eventually divided.

It kept the integrity of nations, as a people, as kin.

The genealogies also then served a purpose, bringing us to Christ's human family being perfect in its generations as it is given in the Gospel. And the real jubilee being the ultimate sabbath, which is Jesus.

The elegance and perfection of this law shouldn't be lost in the allegory or spiritual application, however. It really is the way that we should live, even today.

teachings.title: Eye for eye is God's law, not Hammurabi's
teachings.summary: Eye for eye is God's just law for magistrates, while Jesus calls believers personally to mercy, and the two are complementary rather than contradictory.
teachings.text:
The second half of the chapter begins with a narrative of a child of Egyptian heritage born into the Tribe of Dan, blaspheming God, and God's instructions to take him without the camp and those who heard the blasphemy to stone him to death.

God reiterates that even strangers among them are under His law, both to their good, and to their punishment for violating it.

He says His law is justice, that a murderer be put to death. That blemish, or physical harm, be answered in a like manner; breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.

This concept of God's law has been understood for millennia, preserved for all time, but in 1901 a Babylonian relic was found that contained what is called Hammurabi's Code, a list of laws credited to the ancient king by archeologists, which included the eye for an eye form of justice.

During the 20th century, what was part of God's perfect law (repeated from **Exodus 21:24-25**
*Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot*, *Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe*) began to be credited to a man, and after it had permeated culture that the concept of an eye for an eye actually originated from Hammurabi's Code, people began to mistakenly think it wasn't God's perfect law. And once they'd managed to mislead people with that, they then began to discredit the concept as barbaric, a remnant of ancient Babylon and not the commandments of God.

And so by the close of the 20th Century, most people had no idea that this was found in scripture, and were taught to think of it as a savage injustice.

If the concept was raised by Christians at all, it was in the context of **Matthew 5:38-39**; *Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.* And this was taught as somehow Jesus contradicting the concept, as if He wasn't the author of it. When Jesus says love thy neighbor, The same people pretend it was a new commandment when it comes from Leviticus as well.

But Jesus calling those who are saved by faith in Him to love even our enemies, to pray for them, to not answer violence with violence, but to show mercy and love to them, isn't saying that the law itself is unjust, for it will be the law in the Millennial Kingdom. He's talking about our hearts storing up wrath, vengeance, and hatred.

Before a magistrate, the eye taken for an eye would still be justice.

**1 Timothy 1:9-11**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

But we who are righteous should forgive those who wronged us and show mercy to those in need. These two concepts aren't contradictory but complimentary.

Our mercy doesn't upend the law. Our being at liberty from the law spiritually means we should be more circumspect in how we view our enemies. Our trust in God for vengeance taking priority over our executing our own wrath.

But if the law demands restitution, so be it. The sword is not wielded in vain.

What those who seek to undermine confidence in scripture do is trust that Christians won't be able to rightly divide the word of God, and this higher level concept would escape us, and lead us to showing perverse judgment.

If you notice, by abandoning the law for the unrighteous, instead of mercy and love and limited restitution to a like-for-like code, we have a "justice system" that either punishes the wrong doer far exceeding what is right in the eyes of God, or not doing anything to rightly punish the wicked and protect the innocent. Those that deserve death still live, often freed to offend again.

teachings.title: Justice in the world, meekness in the believer
teachings.summary: Believers must be meek peacemakers personally while God's law should still be upheld by the state, and ignoring this has left society with neither justice nor mercy.
teachings.text:
The nuance required to understand these differences, The worldly application of biblical principles with people who aren't believers versus how believers should respond personally. This causes confusion for many in other applications such as application of Romans 13 and 14.

Christians are called to be meek, to be peacemakers, to be humble in realizing that our condition is by the grace of God and not of ourselves. To be understanding of our enemies that by love, we may overcome it and bring them to the same peace that we have found in the grace of God.

But that doesn't mean that in this world, God's law shouldn't be upheld. And if we were to stone to death, someone for a capital violation, We should not do so gleefully and with vengeance but with understanding. And after applying just mercy.

By not walking this line, we have a society wherein there is no justice and there is no mercy.

We have courts that are grossly unfair. We have a criminal justice system that can't decide between rehabilitation and punishment and so attains neither.

We don't put to death those who have their own blood upon them. And we lock up people who could have simply worked off the harm they caused. The application of the law becomes arbitrary and capricious rather than circumspect and done with discernment.

teachings.title: The law failed because men failed
teachings.summary: The law failed to produce righteousness because Israel would not execute its judgments, and God's wrath abides on any nation that refuses His statutes.
teachings.text:
We know the law is made to be a schoolmaster to bring Israel to repentance of faith in the Christ to come. That the failing of the law to achieve righteousness wasn't God's fault, but man's.

Because when a man dishonored his father and mother, cursing them, the people didn't put him to death.

Because when a man committed adultery with his neighbor's wife, they weren't put to death.

When a man committed incest, uncovering the nakedness of his own family's women, committing abominations, the people do not put him to death.

When sodomites were found amongst them, men laying with men, abominations to the Lord, the people suffered them to live rather than stoning them to death, their blood being upon them.

Bestiality, incest, the abomination of sex in the blood of menstruation...all these things that God warns nations about eventually are left unchecked by a wicked and perverse generation. The people didn't follow His statutes.

*Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.*

God's wrath abides on a nation that fails to sanctify themselves through his  statutes and judgments. As the nations driven out before the Israelites were condemned. As Israel itself would be. And as nations even to this day find out as the land spews them out for their abominations.

teachings.title: Pride goes before destruction
teachings.summary: Walks through passages on pride and humility (Proverbs 6, James 4, Isaiah 2 and 3) to show that God hates pride, that a proud people who make room for the wicked are brought low, and that the righteous are kept through it.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Proverbs 16:18**
*Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.*

**Job 33:16-18**
 *Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction, That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.*

**Psalm 10:1-5**
*Why standest thou afar off, O Lord? why hidest thou thyself in times of trouble? The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined. For the wicked boasteth of his heart's desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the Lord abhorreth. The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts. His ways are always grievous; thy judgments are far above out of his sight: as for all his enemies, he puffeth at them.
*
**Psalm 36:11**
*Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me.*

**Psalm 73:6**
*Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment.*

**Proverbs 8:13**
*The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.*

The things God hates are the things we are called to hate, and pride is one of the things God hates most. It is why the sodomites use the term. They defy God by announcing their pride, against His judgments, glorying in the unnatural lusts that fuel their abominations. 

God promises His children that the proud will be destroyed, that we will be protected from their evil and violence, because God will have vengeance on them, He will repay.

**James 4:6**
*But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.*

**1 Samuel 2:3**
*Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.*

**Psalm 12:3**
*The Lord shall cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things*

**Psalm 40:4**
*Blessed is that man that maketh the Lord his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.*

**Psalm 119:21**
*Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments*

We are called to be humble. To know our place in things. To trust the judgment of God, and do our best to live by His precepts and honor His commandments. His commandments including not giving respect or honor to the proud, but to hate those cursed into their sin. Reprobates. Given up and given over to a reprobate mind. Rejected of God because His judgments are an offense to them in their pride. That they know better than God. 

**Romans 1:32**
*Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

**Romans 2:2**
*But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.*

**Isaiah 2:12**
*For the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low*

There are so many verses and chapters and stories in the Bible showing how pride and giving room to the wicked, to sodomites and violence, leads to destruction of the people and their being humbled by the Lord. It is one of the major themes of the Bible. It is inescapable. 

**Isaiah 3**
*For, behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water.

2 The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the prudent, and the ancient,

3 The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator.

4 And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.

5 And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.

6 When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand:

7 In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.

8 For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

9 The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.

10 Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

11 Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him.

12 As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.

13 The Lord standeth up to plead, and standeth to judge the people.

14 The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.

15 What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord God of hosts.

16 Moreover the Lord saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:

17 Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will discover their secret parts.

18 In that day the Lord will take away the bravery of their tinkling ornaments about their feet, and their cauls, and their round tires like the moon,

19 The chains, and the bracelets, and the mufflers,

20 The bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands, and the tablets, and the earrings,

21 The rings, and nose jewels,

22 The changeable suits of apparel, and the mantles, and the wimples, and the crisping pins,

23 The glasses, and the fine linen, and the hoods, and the vails.

24 And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty.

25 Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.

26 And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground.*

Note the preaching of Isaiah against Judah and the cause of God's wrath and the curse of His judgement against them. That their pride led them there. *Their tongue and their doings are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of His glory.*..*They declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul!*

To the righteous, who keep their faith in God through this, it shall be well with them. *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.* We shouldn't worry or fear the fall that is coming to our nation for their wickedness and pride. For declaring their sin as Sodom. We will be saved from it, even as we are persecuted for our stedfast faith. 

But woe unto the wicked. They will be rewarded in the manner of their deeds, *receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*

teachings.title: Thou shalt not bow down to graven images
teachings.summary: Idolatry is still sin, and Catholic kneeling, candles and processions before images are worship of idols, a key reason God's wrath is on America and Europe.
teachings.text:
Just a side note, the New Testament commands we flew idols. That Idolatry is still a sin. *Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold* still stands.

*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.*

Note also, that this commandment, which Catholics omit from their version, for obvious reasons, has 'bowing down,' the literal meaning of worship. Those kneeling before idols are worshiping. Those lighting a candle in front of them are serving. The feasts of the "saints," where the people carry an idol through the streets, and give service unto it are a blasphemy.

And God promises to strike a nation, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon them unto the third and fourth generation.

If you want to know one of the prime reasons God's wrath is upon the United States, and Europe, it is for allowing this blasphemy to continue for 1500yrs.

teachings.title: Jethro's counsel to delegate judgment
teachings.summary: God approves delegated authority, so believers should know His word for themselves, with fathers, pastors and deacons answering to Christ, a pattern of the Millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
But regardless of all that, and regardless of the marriage troubles Moses may have had, Jethro in his visit gives good advice to his son-in-law Moses.

Moses has 600,000 men, plus women and children in the mixed multitudes encamped with him. 12 tribes of Israel, come out of Egypt, and as their leader, he must sit in judgment. Jethro observes the long lines and the grind of dealing with them all that Moses faces and offers good advice.

*The thing that thou doest is not good.*
*Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.*
*Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do. Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.*

God blesses this arrangement, and Moses takes to it and does as Jethro advised.

We see other times, in other places throughout the Bible that God approves of delegation of authority. He wants the people to know His ways and laws and the ordinances of remembrance, that in what they do they know the next right choice to make.

We are to know the word of God that we can know ourselves what His will is. Without needing someone micromanaging and interpreting scripture, to constantly make decisions for us on normal matters.

God then sets up captains over people, to judge matters for their people. By 10s, 100s and 1,000s. And a leader who answers to God, for the tougher matters of judgment. Thus will it be in the Millennium. Those who showed judgment and did great things for the Lord will be given much in the Kingdom. Those good and faithful servants will be made rulers, as Jesus described in the parable of the servants.

We see the wisdom in this arrangement. The way it maximizes the ability to serve God and edify people. And this exists today through God's word; the priesthood of believers, the husband/father of the home, the local pastor, his helpers the deacons or elders, all answering to Jesus. It is the form of Christian nationalism that we should seek.

teachings.title: God judges nations; Jewish identity is rejecting Christ
teachings.summary: God is no respecter of persons in offering salvation but judges nations collectively, and the Jews' identity rests on rejecting Christ, so they are given over as in Romans 1.
teachings.text:
God is not a respecter of persons, the Bible says repeatedly. He does not care if you are great or small, rich or poor. Man or woman, Greek or Jew, where you're from or who your parents are. He gives us all the same offer of salvation and adoption in Christ. As individuals we have free will.

God does judge nations. He does favor some over others at times, and destroys many who go too far astray. He curses the land stained by blood of violence. Sodomy. Fornication. Of people, collectively, to the fourth generation.
